\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{امکان} (imkān)}{امکان (imkān)}]{\ur{امکان} (imkān) — a possibility; a chance}

\label{lesson:UR-C361-imkan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a sin, then the Urdu for to hold on to.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{امکان}}
\textbf{\ur{امکان}} — \emph{imkān} — \textquotedblleft{}a possibility; a chance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بادل} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{بارش} \ur{کا} \ur{امکان} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bādal haiṅ to bārish kā imkān hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there are clouds, there is a chance of rain.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{امکان}} (\emph{imkān}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{imkān}, \textquotedblleft{}possibility\textquotedblright{}, of the same family as \textbf{\ur{ممکن}}, \textquotedblleft{}possible\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imkān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imkān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bādal haiṅ to bārish kā imkān hai.} — If there are clouds, there is a chance of rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a sin, then the Urdu for to hold on to, then say \emph{imkān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{امکان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A possibility; a chance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گنجائش} (gunjāish)}{گنجائش (gunjāish)}]{\ur{گنجائش} (gunjāish) — room; scope (for)}

\label{lesson:UR-C361-gunjaish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to hold on to, then the Urdu for a possibility.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گنجائش}}
\textbf{\ur{گنجائش}} — \emph{gunjāish} — \textquotedblleft{}room; scope (for)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{میں} \ur{گنجائش} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{بھی} \ur{آؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar gāṛī meṅ gunjāish hai to maiṅ bhī āūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گنجائش}} (\emph{gunjāish}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{gunjāyish}, \textquotedblleft{}room, capacity\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اتفاق} (ittifāq)}{اتفاق (ittifāq)}]{\ur{اتفاق} (ittifāq) — chance; a coincidence}

\label{lesson:UR-C361-ittifaq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a possibility, then the Urdu for scope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اتفاق}}
\textbf{\ur{اتفاق}} — \emph{ittifāq} — \textquotedblleft{}chance; a coincidence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{اتفاق} \ur{سے} \ur{وہ} \ur{مل} \ur{گیا} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{بتاؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ittifāq se voh mil gayā to maiṅ batāūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{اتفاق}} (\emph{ittifāq}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ittifāq}, \textquotedblleft{}a coming together, agreement\textquotedblright{}: things that happen to come together.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{احتمال} (ehtimāl)}{احتمال (ehtimāl)}]{\ur{احتمال} (ehtimāl) — a probability (formal)}

\label{lesson:UR-C361-ehtimal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for scope, then the Urdu for a coincidence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{احتمال}}
\textbf{\ur{احتمال}} — \emph{ehtimāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a probability (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تیز} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{طوفان} \ur{کا} \ur{احتمال} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar hawā tez huī to tūfān kā ehtimāl hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{احتمال}} (\emph{ehtimāl}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iḥtimāl}, \textquotedblleft{}bearing, enduring; likelihood\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بیتنا} (bītnā)}{بیتنا (bītnā)}]{\ur{بیتنا} (bītnā) — to go by (of time); to pass}

\label{lesson:UR-C361-bitna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a coincidence, then the Urdu for a probability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بیتنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بیتنا}} — \emph{bītnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to go by (of time); to pass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وقت} \ur{بیت} \ur{گیا} \ur{تو} \ur{کچھ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہو} \ur{سکے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar vaqt bīt gayā to kuchh nahīṅ ho sake gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the time slips by, nothing can be done.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سال} \ur{جلدی} \ur{بیت} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh sāl jaldī bīt gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بیتنا}} (\emph{bītnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bītnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass (of time)\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vṛttá}, \textquotedblleft{}turned, passed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12069).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bītnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar vaqt bīt gayā to kuchh nahīṅ ho sake gā.} — If the time slips by, nothing can be done.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a coincidence, then the Urdu for a probability, then say \emph{bītnā} again
\end{itemize}
